subject: Compliance add-ons: amortization vs. staged credits — proposal for HearthWell
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Parker <danielle@hearthwell.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compliance add-ons: amortization vs. staged credits — proposal for HearthWell

Hi Danielle,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to hear more about HearthWell's rollout plans for clinician-facing workflows. As promised, attached is an initial pricing workup that breaks our compliance/security add-ons into three components: Audit Logs (retention tiers), Keystore (managed KMS vs dedicated HSM seat), and Data Residency (US-only vs US+EU).

High-level options in the workbook:
- Option A (amortized implementation): one-time implementation fee, smaller ongoing surcharge.
- Option B (staged credits): reduce upfront cash by converting a portion of the implementation fee into credits earned over 12 months tied to usage/commits.
- Option C (pass-through): minimal Redwood margin for HSM seats, customer pays third-party HSM license directly.

Key assumptions called out in the sheet: 7-year audit retention for clinical records, HIPAA scope to cover PHI processing, and EU region readiness as a follow-on phase.

Next steps I'd propose:
1) you confirm preference (A/B/C) or tell us a mix;
2) we loop in Markus (security engineering) and Ben (commercial/finance) to finalize amortization schedule;
3) we ship a revised term sheet + SOW for procurement review.

Attachments: HearthWell-compliance-workup-20270909.xlsx (workbook), Redwood-compliance-term-sheet-v2.pdf (term-sheet stub)

Would Thursday next week at 10am PT work for a final review?

Thanks,

--
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Danielle Parker <danielle@hearthwell.com>

Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compliance add-ons: amortization vs. staged credits — proposal for HearthWell

Hi Laura,

Appreciate the workbook — that format is helpful. A few clarifying items from procurement and infra:

- We need a firm breakdown of what drives the implementation fee. Specifically: HSM integration labor, audit-log ingestion pipeline work, and residency provisioning (network peering / routing). Can you itemize those labor buckets?
- For staged credits (Option B) — we need to see the earning triggers. Procurement prefers time-based milestones (e.g., 3/6/12 months) tied to activation, not purely usage thresholds.
- HIPAA scoping: we will require proof of SOC 2 + BAAs in the contract and a separate line item for the BAA execution cost if you plan to charge.
- EU residency: timeline matters. If we plan to go EU in Q2-2028, we want a commitment to region-onboarding SLAs and a one-time provisioning credit if delayed.

One more ask: can you propose a blended list price and a committed discount for a pilot (3 months) vs enterprise (12 months) — procurement needs those two bands.

If you can get us a revised sheet by Monday EOD (our side will review), we can aim to sign the pilot SOW the week after.

Thanks — Danielle
VP, Product Operations
Danielle Parker
Danielle.Parker@hearthwell.com

Subject: Re: Compliance add-ons: amortization vs. staged credits — proposal for HearthWell

Danielle,

Thanks — responding inline and attaching a revised tab called "Procurement-ready" that follows your asks. High-level answers below; see the attached workbook for numeric detail.

Itemized implementation fee (one-time):
- HSM integration (dedicated seat): engineering effort = 80 hours, professional services rate = $250/hr -> $20k.
- Audit-log pipeline (ingest + archive config): 100 hours -> $22.5k.
- Residency provisioning (networking, peering, certs): 40 hours -> $8k.
- Project management and compliance evidence package (SOC2/BAA collection): $5k.
- Total one-time implementation fee (sum): $55.5k (we proposed $60k in workbook to allow a small margin).

Staged credits (Option B) — proposed structure we think matches procurement preference:
- 40% of the implementation fee converted to credits (applied to Redwood invoices).
- Credits vest on time-based milestones: 15% at go-live, 15% at 3 months post-go-live, 10% at 12 months.
- Remaining 60% invoiced upfront or amortized over first 6 months per your AP preference.

HIPAA / BAA:
- Redwood will sign a standard BAA at no additional fee. The "BAA execution cost" line in the workbook was referencing professional services to assist with evidence packaging and audits — we can reclassify that as optional and drop it from the base SOW.

EU residency commitment:
- Target onboarding for an EU region is Q2 2028. If onboarding slips beyond a mutually agreed cutoff (currently June 30, 2028), we propose a $10k provisioning credit to HearthWell. We can add a contractual SLA for onboarding timing in the SOW.

Pricing bands (blended list vs committed pilot/enterprise):
- Pilot (3 mo): 20% list discount from our cataloged add-on rates, no long-term commit required; credits apply but limited to 50% of convertable credit pool.
- Enterprise (12 mo): 30% list discount with a minimum committed spend -> credits as structured above and eligibility for additional volume credits at annual true-up.

Attachments: updated workbook tab (Procurement-ready), revised term-sheet PDF.

Markus + Ben — can you confirm the HSM seat and audit-log labor assumptions look right on your side? If any of that changes materially we’ll update the milestone percentages.

Proposed next step: doodle for Thursday 09/16 at 10am PT to walk procurement and legal through the revised terms.

Thanks,

--
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

If you update the workbook and term sheet to reflect those two items, we can route to legal and procurement and target a pilot SOW signature by 09/24.
